issues.description: Entry-point name mismatch: the problem statement requires the program entry point to be a global symbol named `start_app` (problem_statement.md), but the provided template and solution export and use the symbol `main` instead. In template_repository/helloWorld.asm the file declares `global main` (line 6) and provides a `main:` label (line 8). In solution_repository/helloWorld.asm the file also declares `global main` (line 6) while defining a separate non-exported label `start_app:` (line 8). This inconsistent naming will confuse students about which symbol to implement as the entry point and can cause the final binary to use the wrong entry symbol.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the required entry-point name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the problem statement to require `main` as the entry point, or (B) change both assembly files to export and use `start_app` as the entrypoint. Concretely, if keeping `start_app`: replace `global main` with `global start_app` and ensure the entry label is `start_app` (or rename `main:` to `start_app:`) in both template_repository/helloWorld.asm and solution_repository/helloWorld.asm.

issues.description: Visibility mismatch for the required entry symbol: the problem statement requires `start_app` to be the global entry point, but in the solution file `start_app:` is defined (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 8) without being declared global. Instead the solution file declares `global main` (line 6). Because `start_app` is not exported with `global`, it will not serve as the external entry symbol expected by the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the declared global symbol matches the required entry point. If the intended entrypoint is `start_app`, add `global start_app` to the top of the assembly files (and remove or replace `global main`), and make `start_app:` the actual entry label. Alternatively, update the problem statement to require `main` as the entrypoint to match the existing files.
